THE CHINESE COURTS IN FRENCH CONCESSION

A certain party has long desired to seize
control of the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court and the
Shanghai 2nd Special District Court in the French Concession.
Rumours were prevalent to the effect that the two Courts
would be undergoing a rapid change in a day or two, but they
have been proved to be untrue.
Yesterday the two Courts were guarded by
policemen sent by the French Police, cases were being heard
and the entire staff of the two Courts was at work as usual.
Yesterday the Court authorities stated to
a reporter that they had received orders from the Ministry of
Justice to the effect that the Ministry had received
information about the rumours in Shanghai but that the two
Courts should continue at their work as usual.
According to information secured from a
reliable source, a certain party recently showed an increasing
desire to take over the control of the Chinese Courts in the
French Concession and it is believed that it had already
expressed its desire to the French authorities on several
occasions. The two Courts were formed following the conclusion
of an agreement between China and France and no local body
has the authority to decide whether the present situation
should be maintained or not.
It is learned that the local French officials
recently referred the present situation to the French
Ambassador who is now in Chungking. As his decision will have
an effect upon Sino-French relations, he has carefully
to examine the question. The Chinese Government will oppose
any movement that is liable to prejudice the judicial rights
of China During the diplomatic negotiations, no untoward
incidents are expected to occur.
The Ministry of Justice of the Chungking
Government yesterday sent a telegram to President Yang (杨)
of the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court ordering all the
Judges of the two Courts to continue at their work and not to
abandon their post until compelled. Arrangements have been
made already in case Judges are compelled to leave their
posts; the payment of their salaries will, however, be issued.
It is rumoured that M. E. d'Hooghe, Judicial
Councillor of the French Municipal Council, has informed Yang
Bang (杨邦), President of the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court, that the French authorities are no longer prepared
to assist in maintaining the present status of the Chinese
Courts.
A spokesman of the French Consulate states:
"A parley has been going on for a long time in Chungking
between M. Henry Cosme, French Ambassador, and the Chinese
Government. No developments have taken place in Shanghai."
It was rumoured yesterday that the French
Police has detailed additional policemen and armoured cars
to guard the Shanghai 2nd Special District Court but the
French Police deny the report. A senior official of the French
Police told a reporter that since the outbreak of the 1937
hostilities, policemen had always been detailed to guard
the Shanghai 2nd Special District Court. The patrolling of
armoured cars in the French Concession started at the
beginning of the peace. In view of all this, the situation
over the two Courts in the French Concession was nothing
out of the ordinary yesterday.

法租界内的中国法院

某方长期以来一直企图夺取法租界内江苏高等法院第三分院和上海第二特区地方法院的控制权。谣言盛行，称这两所法院在一两天内将发生急剧变化，但已被证明不实。

昨日，这两所法院由法国警察派出的巡捕守卫，案件正在审理，两所法院的全体职员照常工作。

昨日，法院当局向记者表示，他们收到司法部的命令，称司法部已获悉上海的有关谣言，但两所法院应继续照常工作。

据可靠消息来源获悉，某方最近表现出越来越强烈的接管法租界内中国法院控制权的愿望，据信它已多次向法国当局表达了这一愿望。这两所法院是在中法达成协议后成立的，任何地方机构都无权决定是否维持现状。

据悉，法国地方官员最近已将当前局势提交给目前在重庆的法国大使。由于他的决定将影响中法关系，他必须仔细审查这一问题。中国政府将反对任何可能损害中国司法权利的行动。在外交谈判期间，预计不会发生不幸事件。

重庆政府司法部昨日致电江苏高等法院第三分院院长杨（Yang），命令两所法院的所有法官继续工作，除非被迫否则不得离职。若法官被迫离职，已作出安排；但其薪金仍将发放。

谣传法国公董局司法顾问 E. d'Hooghe 先生（音译）已通知江苏高等法院第三分院院长杨邦（Yang Bang），法国当局不再准备协助维持中国法院的现状。

法国领事馆发言人称：“法国大使 Henry Cosme 先生（音译）与中国政府在重庆进行了长时间的会谈。上海方面没有发生任何变化。”

昨日有谣言称，法国警察已增派额外警力和装甲车守卫上海第二特区地方法院，但法国警察否认了这一报道。法国警察的一名高级官员告诉记者，自1937年战事爆发以来，一直派遣巡捕守卫上海第二特区地方法院。装甲车在法租界的巡逻始于和平初期。鉴于此，昨日法租界两所法院的局势并无异常。

Shanghai 2nd Special Area District Court and the 3rd
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court - possible transfer
to the Nanking Government.

For some time past, the Japanese authorities in
Shanghai have been contemplating the taking over of the
Chinese judicial organs in the International Settlement
and the French Concession, but because of the numerous
difficulties attending such a scheme nothing tangible
in this direction has ever been attempted.

However, on the capitulation of the French
Government in the European War, the Japanese authorities
again have taken the matter up, this time it would
appear seriously as regards the French Concession and have
lately brought pressure to bear upon the authorities
of the French Concession. Information has been obtained
that negotiations between the Japanese Authorities
acting on behalf of the Nanking Government and the
French authorities have been in progress and are
reaching the final stage whereby it is expected that the
Shanghai 2nd Special Area District Court and the 3rd
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court will be transferred to
those authorities, the date given being the beginning of

recently hinted to the Court officials that the local
French authorities, on account of the present circum-
stances, would not be in a position to maintain the status
quo of these courts and that negotiations between the
Court officials and representatives of the Nanking
Government are in progress. All the officials and other

As far as can be ascertained the drafting

It is correct that Hsia is anxious to seize

As indicated in a previous report, force may be used

Hsia Chi Feng, the new Minister of Foreign
Affairs who took up his post about ten days ago, is not
very popular with the community of Shanghai. In 1916
he went to France as interpreter to the Labour Corps.
He returned to China after the armistice, bringing
with him a French wife. The latter deserted him after
several years. Hsia joined the Eastern Times as a
reporter in 1919, proceeded to Europe in 1921 as
special correspondent for that journal and at the
same time served as unofficial publicity agent for the
Chinese delegation to the League of Nations.
He returned to Shanghai in 1928 and holding an
honorary position as advisor to the Minister of Foreign
Affairs he became almost penniless and was associated
with the Frenchtown fraternity especially with the late
Tang Chia Pang who was killed outside the Great World
a few years ago.

据查，起草关于在租界确立维新政府“法律权利”的法案仅仅是外交部长夏奇峰（Hsia Chi Feng）的宣传手段。夏奇峰急于夺取租界和法租界内的中国法院，这一点属实，因为一旦掌握法院，维新政府便能轻易对租界内的金融和商业组织行使有效管辖权。正如前一份报告所指出的，如果不可避免，可能会使用武力。

新任外交部长夏奇峰于约十天前就职，在上海社群中并不受欢迎。1916年，他作为劳工团的翻译前往法国。停战后返回中国，带回一位法国妻子。数年后，该女子离他而去。1919年，夏加入《字林西报》（Eastern Times）担任记者，1921年作为该报特约通讯员前往欧洲，同时担任中国出席国际联盟代表团非官方宣传代理人。他于1928年返回上海，担任外交部顾问这一荣誉职位，几乎身无分文，并与法租界帮派人士交往密切，特别是与几年前在大世界门外被杀的唐嘉邦（Tang Chia Pang）关系匪浅。

NANKING, Aug. 22.—A bill for
the purpose of seeking the estab-

ernment's "legal rights" in the

To Take Steps
Officials of the Foreign Ministry
will take immediate steps to re-
cover "legal rights" in the Inter-
national Settlement after the bill is
passed at an administrative meet-
ing Thursday, it was announced
today.
"The Ministry of Foreign Affairs
is determined to effect a solution
not only of the Jessfield Road in-
cident but also of the entire Set-
tlement questioned," Mr. Hsia Chi-
feng, Minister of Foreign Affairs,

A Naughty Word
"An outrageous incident of this
kind is certain to lead to further
massacres of Chinese people by
Shanghai municipal police unless
a fundamental solution of it is
effected.
"This incident is an insult to
the Reformed Government. At
the same time it is a provocative
action which tends to lead to
similar incidents.
"We have had two urgent min-
isterial conferences and dispatch-
ed an official to Shanghai to in-
quire into the facts of the
incident."

taking active steps to marshal
public support behind the Reform-
ed Government in its plans to
seek a solution of the Interna-
tional Settlement question. The
society sent telegrams to many
sections of the country.

claration that it was launching a
movement to "mobilize the people"
to recover the International Set-
tlement.

南京起草法案谋求
国际租界法律权利

（多梅特）
南京，8月22日电。—昨日，在一次外交部官员第二次会议上，起草了一项旨在寻求确立维新政府在上海公共租界“法律权利”的法案。
此举与上周六晚上海西区发生的枪击事件有关。
将采取行动
今日宣布，在该法案于周四行政会议通过后，外交部官员将立即采取措施，收回在国际租界的“法律权利”。
“外交部决心不仅解决极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）事件，还要解决整个受质疑的租界问题，”外交部长夏奇峰先生宣称。
一个刺耳的字眼
“如果不从根本上解决此类恶劣事件，必然会导致上海工部局警察进一步屠杀中国人。
“此事件是对维新政府的侮辱。同时，这也是一种挑衅行为，倾向于引发类似事件。
“我们已召开两次紧急部长级会议，并派遣一名官员前往上海调查事件真相。”
与此同时，大民会正积极采取措施，动员公众支持维新政府寻求解决国际租界问题的计划。该协会向全国许多地区发送了电报。
大民会发表声明，称正在发起一场“动员民众”收回国际租界的运动。

Sir,

At 3.25 p.m. on August 6, 1939, two telephone
messages were received from the S.S.D. Court Nos. 160
and 2159 respectively, reporting the presence of
five plain-clothes Japanese outside the main gate of the Court.
It was stated that they were taking photographs of the building and had
endeavoured to enter.

Inspector Taylor, P.C. 214 and P.C. 215 under my instructions
promptly proceeded to the scene whilst F. Newell, Charge
Room Sergeant, telephoned Hongkew Station for the assistance
of a Japanese detective. S.I. Brown also attended.

On arrival five plain-clothed Japanese were observed out-
side the main gate, all of whom it was learnt arrived in a
Private M/Car bearing S.M.C. Lic. No. 4921, and Shanghai City
Government Lic. No. 117. One of them, who was seen to be in
possession of a "Graflex" camera, had, according to P.C. 215, Heise,
taken several photographs of the building despite his, the
officer's, protest.

First attempts on the part of investigating officers to
obtain the nature of their business proved unsuccessful as they
were reluctant to impart any information. Eventually, however,
D.S.I. Chu ascertained from one of them, who spoke Chinese,
that they were from the Japanese Gendarmerie Haining Road and
that they wished to enter the S.S.D. Court to interview Judge
Tse. Accordingly they were informed that the Judge did not
attend the S.S.D. Court in the afternoon, but that they could
most likely be interviewed at the Weihaiwei Road offices. They
were also instructed to apply to Police Headquarters for
assistance, should they at any time wish to operate in the

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
                                S.2 Special Branch.  Station
                        REPORT
                                            Date .. July 31,   19 39.
Subject..................Alleged Japanese anxiety over the question of
.........................the Shanghai Special District Court....................
Made by................................Forwarded by....................................

According to information received from
pro-Japanese elements, the Japanese Authorities in
Shanghai held a conference sometime ago to discuss the
question of the Shanghai Special District Court.
        The military authorities pointed out,
according to the report, that the neutrality of the
Settlement could not be maintained with the existence
of the Court which is a "Chungking" organization.
Despite all difficulties even at the cost of using
force, the Court must be restored to the Reformed
Government.
        The civil authorities, however, did not
favour the use of force but preferred negotiations with
the Consular Body.  The difference of opinion was
referred to the Tokyo Government which gave instructions
that peaceful negotiations be first taken up with the
Senior Consul. It is understood that one Tatsuno, former
Director of the Mining Administration in Manchukuo and
ex-advisor to the Shanghai City Government, has made
certain suggestions to the Japanese authorities that in
order to avoid opposition from the Settlement authorities
the names of new judges to be appointed to the Court
should be first referred to the Consular Body for approval
and if necessary cases to be tried with the assistance of
a jury.  Tatsuno claims to know Messrs. Arnhold and
Fessenden.
Certified true copy.
J. F. Lovell

Confiden  ial:

Shanghai, ay 26th, 1938.

ear ir,

I have obtained a very important news from
my relative who is workin in the New Asia) pertaining
to the First District Court. As it concerns the whole
Chinese nationality in the Settlement feel it is my
duty to report to you in order to enable you to take
necessary steps. The information is as following:

r. Lin who supposed to be the resident of
the Court has seen the Chairman of the Consul
Body and the British Consul General. They
promised him to hold a meeting tomorrow and
to give a definit answer whether they allow
him to take over the Court or not. But
the Japanese Military and the New Asia people
predicted that the answer would not be very
favourable. So they decided to carry out the
undermentioned steps should they not allow
Mr. Lin to take over the court:-

1. That they will through grenade in Nanking
Road as that the Japanese can blame the Authority
of the Settlement and occupy Nanking Road until
the Court is handed over.
2. That they will send out member of the Huang
Tao Association to kill all the important people
of the Court whose addresses have already been
known by them.
3. That they will occupy the Ward Jail on the
ground that among the prisoners there are many
anti-Japanese elements who were slightly sentenced.

机密：

上海，1938 年 5 月 26 日。

亲爱的先生：

我从在新亚（New Asia，音译）工作的亲戚那里
获得了一条非常重要的消息，涉及第一特区法院。
由于此事关系到租界内全体中国籍居民，我觉得
有责任向您报告，以便您采取必要措施。情报如下：

据称是法院居民的林先生（Mr. Lin，音译）
会见了领事团主席和英国总领事。他们
答应他明天举行会议，并就是否允许
他接管法院给予明确答复。但是
日本军方和新亚人士预测，答复不会很
有利。因此，他们决定，如果不允许
林先生接管法院，将采取以下步骤：-

1. 他们将在南京路投掷手榴弹，以便日本人
可以指责租界当局，并占领南京路，直到
法院移交为止。
2. 他们将派出黄道会成员杀害法院所有重要人物，
这些人的住址他们已知晓。
3. 他们将以囚犯中有许多被判轻刑的反日分子为由，
占领华德路监狱。
